Current (Finco Services, Inc.) is an American financial services and software development company (FinTech) based in New York City[1] which provides mobile banking services through its partner banks, Choice Financial Group and Cross River Bank.
The company offers spending accounts, which include early access to paychecks, fee-free overdraft, secured credit building, earned wage access, savings boosts up to 4%, fee-free ATMs, cryptocurrency and redeemable points for cash back. Current’s mobile banking services do not have annual fees, overdraft fees or minimum balance requirements.[2][3][4]
Current provides services through its mobile app, and has no physical branches. Account-holders are issued Visa debit cards or credit cards, and have access to an online banking system accessible via the mobile app for Android or iOS.
History
[edit]Stuart Sopp and Trevor Marshall founded Current in 2015 in New York City to provide alternative banking services to traditional banks.[5][6]
Current bases their banking platform on technology called the Current Core. This system lowered the cost of maintaining accounts in comparison to traditional banks built on legacy infrastructure. This allows Current to provide service to customers at a lower cost than traditional banks, and thus eliminate or reduce fees charged to customers.[7]
In 2024, Current was named to CNBC’s ‘The World’s Top 250 Fintech Companies’.[8]
In January 2025, Current became a member of the American Fintech Council.[9]
Product Launches
[edit]Current's first product, a debit card for teens controlled by parents, launched in May 2017.[10]
Current launched its personal accounts for adults in February 2019, which featured early access to wages with direct deposit, fee-free overdraft (up to $200), no minimum balance requirements, and instant removals of gas holds that stations put on debit cards.[11]
In 2020, Current became the first U.S. based consumer fintech to launch a points reward system based on debit, which allows its members to earn points redeemable for cash back in their Current accounts.[12]
In September 2020, Current launched an add cash feature through its partnership with InComm, giving its members the ability to add cash to their Current accounts at over 60,000 stores nationwide that is then instantly available in their Current accounts.[13]
In January 2022, Current launched a 4% APY savings product.[14]
In October 2022, Current launched crypto trading without fees[15] in partnership with Zero Hash, giving its over four million members access to buy and sell dozens of coins on its platform without paying trading fees and with instant liquidity from trades.
Also in October 2022, Current announced it was now doing its own processing directly with Visa.[16]
In August 2023, Current launched a secured credit building card in partnership with Cross River Bank. Current members can build their credit histories through a single spending balance on Current’s platform. The secured charge card connects to a members’ available spending balance.[17]
In early 2024, Current launched Paycheck Advance, its earned wage access product, allowing members to access up to $750 of an upcoming paycheck in advance without any mandatory fees or credit checks.[18]
Growth and development
[edit]Account growth
[edit]By December 2022, Current had over four million accounts.[19]
Other milestones included nearly three million accounts in April 2021,[20] two million accounts in November 2022 (doubling its member base in less than six months),[21] and one million accounts in June 2020, less than a year and half after launching its personal accounts.[22]
Starting in April, Current added over 100,000 new members each month in 2020.[23]
Operations
[edit]Business model
[edit]Current has no physical branch locations and does not charge overdraft fees or have a minimum balance requirement.[24] Account holders are issued Visa debit or credit cards and have access to Current's online banking system via its mobile app for iOS or Android.
Current has a spend-based business model, earning revenue from interchange. Current Accounts have no monthly account fees.[25]
In March 2025, Current announced the release of a new case study from Datos Insights titled ‘Foregoing BaaS: How Owning the Core Fuels Current’s Success,’ which concluded Current’s choice to build and not buy the core banking platform has been a defining factor in the company’s growth and success.[26]
Patents
[edit]On December 12, 2019, the company applied for patent 16424341 / 20190378121, "Cryptographic Technology Platform And Methods For Providers To Enable Users To Monetize Their Data" that would cryptographically give end-users, i.e., customers, an option to maintain complete personal data privacy or opt to monetize all or part of it.[27]
FDIC Insurance
[edit]Current accounts are insured up to the standard maximum deposit insurance amount of $250,000 through its bank partners, Choice Financial, Member FDIC and/or Cross River Bank, Member FDIC.
Current announced it had no plans at the present time to pursue its own bank charter in October 2020.[28]
Response to the COVID-19 pandemic
[edit]In April 2020, Current was the first neobank to receive government stimulus payments for its customers under the CARES Act, and used its own balance sheet to credit all member accounts immediately, which was five days faster than most incumbent banks.[29]
A few days later, Current announced most of the stimulus funds were being used on food, groceries, gas and day-to-day living costs. Over 45 percent of the first funds were spent within five days.[30]
In December 2020, Current was again the first neobank to credit government stimulus payments, receiving and crediting the funds just hours after the Treasury Secretary announced their distribution, using its own balance sheet to credit the funds for all member accounts immediately.[31]
In March 2021, Current again credited all government stimulus payments five days faster than traditional banks, using its own balance sheet to credit funds for all member accounts immediately.[32]

So, you’ve probably heard the buzzword floating around: Pay on Demand Payroll. What exactly is it? Simply put, Pay on demand payroll, also known as Earned Wage Access EWA, is a financial service that gives you, the employee, the ability to access a portion of your wages after you’ve earned them but before your official, scheduled payday. Think of it as hitting the “fast forward” button on your paycheck for the work you’ve already completed.
It’s completely changing the game because it flips the old two-week waiting cycle on its head. Instead of waiting for a bi-weekly or monthly paycheck, you can use an app—usually provided by a third-party partner your employer works with—to request a payout. The provider fronts you the money, and then they settle up with your employer on payday, deducting the advance from your final check.
This isn’t some complicated loan or an advance from your boss. it’s your money when you need it. It’s a huge shift, especially in a world where everything else is instantaneous—we can order food, a ride, or anything else with a tap, so why should access to your own pay be any different?
Here’s a quick summary of what this is all about:
- What it is: A financial wellness benefit allowing access to accrued earned wages before the official payday.
- Other Names: Earned Wage Access EWA, Instant Pay, On-Demand Pay, Daily Pay.
- How it Works The Short Guide:
- You Work: You put in a shift, and the EWA system tracks your hours and how much you’ve earned.
- You Request: You open the provider’s app and request an early payout for a portion of your earned wages usually a cap is set.
- You Get Paid: The funds are instantly or quickly transferred to your bank account, often for a small flat fee.
- Repayment is Automatic: On your next regular payday, your employer deducts the advanced amount plus any fees from your full paycheck before it’s deposited.
- The Big Deal: The Earned Wage Access market is booming, expected to grow at a Compound Annual Growth Rate CAGR of 25.7% through 2034, showing just how much people want this flexibility. Nearly 95% of employees want this kind of access!

Why Pay on Demand Is Exploding Right Now
The sudden explosion of on-demand pay isn’t just a tech fad. it’s a direct response to how modern life and money management have changed. People don’t live on a two-week financial calendar anymore, especially with the cost of living feeling like it’s constantly going up.
The Real-Life Problem EWA Solves
You know how it is: you’re paid on the 15th, and then on the 20th, a surprise bill pops up—maybe it’s a crucial car repair or an unexpected medical expense. Without EWA, your only options are usually pretty rough:
- Overdraft Fees: You use your debit card, and your bank slaps you with a fee for spending money you technically haven’t received yet.
- Payday Loans: You turn to high-interest lenders that can trap you in a cycle of debt. This is what EWA is specifically designed to help you avoid.
- Late Fees: You simply can’t pay a bill on time and get hit with penalties.
Earned Wage Access eliminates that agonizing gap. It gives you the liquidity to handle those real-life, immediate expenses with your own money instead of borrowing someone else’s. Research has even shown that employees using on-demand pay saw nearly 50% fewer monthly overdraft fees, which is a huge win for financial stability.
How Earned Wage Access Actually Works Under the Hood
When you’re looking at your own bank account, the process seems magical: you tap a button and money appears. But for your employer’s payroll team, there’s a lot of smart technology at work. It’s important to understand the model being used.
The Two Main Models of On-Demand Pay
Right now, there are generally two ways this technology is deployed. Most of the time, the one offered by your employer is the safest and most streamlined. Building Infrastructure Examples for the Modern Era
1. The Employer-Integrated Model Most Common
This is the most common and arguably the best for employees.
- The Partnership: Your employer partners with a dedicated EWA vendor like DailyPay, Payactiv, or Paycor.
- The Integration: The EWA provider’s software seamlessly connects with your employer’s existing payroll and time-tracking systems. This is key because the system knows exactly how many hours you’ve worked and how much you’ve earned, down to the penny.
- The Transaction: When you request an advance, the third-party EWA provider sends you the funds. Your employer’s cash flow isn’t immediately impacted, and the EWA provider essentially acts as a short-term funder.
- Repayment: On your normal payday, your employer sends the full paycheck amount to the EWA provider, who deducts the advance and any small transaction fee, and then sends the remaining balance to you.
2. The Direct-to-Consumer D2C Model
This model doesn’t require employer integration, and you interact directly with the app, but it comes with a few more risks.
- The Process: Apps like this ask you to link your bank account and sometimes your work schedule. They try to estimate your earned wages based on your direct deposit history.
- The Risk: Since they aren’t fully integrated with your company’s payroll, there’s a higher chance of inaccuracies. Also, these services can sometimes be riskier when it comes to fees, with some direct-to-consumer models having an effective Annual Percentage Rate APR that can be alarmingly high—sometimes over 300%. That’s why sticking to an employer-sponsored EWA benefit is highly recommended.
The Big Benefits of On-Demand Pay for Everyone
This isn’t just a perk. it’s a strategic advantage for employers and a financial lifeline for employees. When you look at the numbers, it’s easy to see why.
For Employees: Taking Control of Your Money
The biggest advantage here is moving from a reactive financial life to a proactive one.
- Slashed Financial Stress: This is the most powerful benefit. When you’re not worried about making it to the next paycheck, you’re happier, and you can focus better at work. This isn’t just feel-good talk. 80% of employers who offer EWA say it has improved the mental health of their teams.
- Avoiding High-Interest Traps: As we talked about, EWA is a fantastic, ethical alternative to high-interest payday loans or constantly incurring bank overdraft fees. Instead of crippling interest, you pay a small, one-time fee for the instant transfer, which is a much, much better deal.
- Better Budgeting: When you have a real-time view of your earnings, it’s easier to manage your budget and know exactly where you stand, rather than waiting two weeks for a lump sum you’ve already mentally spent.
- No Credit Checks or Debt: Since you are accessing money you have already earned, EWA providers don’t run credit checks, and it doesn’t create traditional debt.
For Employers: Boosting Your Business and Talent Pool

The Potential Pitfalls: What to Watch Out For
Now, let’s be real—nothing is perfect. While EWA is a great tool, it’s important to acknowledge the potential downsides, especially from a financial discipline standpoint.
The Employee’s Trap: The “Half-Check” Cycle
The number one concern, and one you need to be very mindful of, is the cycle of dependence.
- Smaller Paychecks: If you consistently take out advances, your final, regular paycheck will be significantly smaller. If you get paid $1,500 and take out $500 early, that next payday is going to feel like a $1,000 check, which can make it hard to cover big, fixed monthly expenses like rent or a car payment. You might then be forced to take another advance almost immediately, starting a tough cycle.
- Impulsive Spending: Having constant access to funds can undermine long-term financial planning if you don’t have good budgeting habits. It’s easy to treat your earned wages as a limitless resource for non-essentials.
Our Advice: Use EWA only for true emergencies or a small buffer. Don’t treat it as a lifestyle change. Always aim to save enough so you don’t need to touch your earned wages early.
The Employer’s Headache: Admin and Compliance
For the company offering this benefit, the complexities mainly revolve around the back-office process.
- Integration Challenges: While many providers integrate seamlessly, not every payroll system is perfect. Integrating a new third-party EWA platform can introduce complexity and potential for errors, especially in calculating gross wages, deductions, and taxes on a variable pay schedule.
- Regulatory Uncertainty: This is the big one. Regulators at the state and federal level are still trying to figure out if EWA is technically a “loan” or not. If it’s classified as a loan, EWA providers could be subjected to strict lending laws, which could change the fee structure and how the services operate. It’s an area, and companies must ensure they partner with a provider who stays compliant with all the latest rules.

Frequently Asked Questions
What is the difference between Pay on Demand and a Payday Loan?
Pay on Demand EWA is fundamentally different from a payday loan because you are accessing money you have already earned through your work, not borrowing future income or a new line of credit. Payday loans are high-interest loans that charge you interest, can damage your credit, and often trap borrowers in a debt cycle. EWA typically charges a small, flat transaction fee like an ATM fee for instant access, and the money is simply deducted from your next paycheck, with no credit implications.
Is Earned Wage Access considered a loan by regulators?
The legal classification of EWA is currently unsettled. Historically, it has often not been considered a loan because it’s access to existing property earned wages, not borrowed money. However, in the US, some states and federal regulatory bodies, like the CFPB, have released proposed rules and opinions that controversially classify it as a form of credit, which has created regulatory uncertainty. The is still , but most employer-integrated services are designed to operate ethically and avoid the issues associated with traditional lending. How much of my earned wages can I access early?
The amount you can access varies by the EWA provider and your employer’s specific policy. Most services will cap the amount to a portion of your accrued wages, often limiting it to around 50% of your earned net pay for the pay period to ensure you still have enough left in your final check for taxes and essential expenses. Some providers may allow up to 100% depending on the company’s agreement.
Are there fees involved with Pay on Demand payroll?
Yes, there are typically fees, but they are usually a small, flat fee—often $3 to $5—for instant fund transfers. Many EWA providers also offer a no-fee option for transfers that take 1 to 3 business days, similar to a standard ACH bank transfer. The employer-integrated model is designed to be affordable, unlike the high-interest rates of alternative lending products.
Does using EWA affect my credit score?
No. Using an employer-sponsored Earned Wage Access service does not involve credit checks, and it does not affect your credit score in any way. The transactions are considered an adjustment to your payroll, not a loan that is reported to credit bureaus.
Who pays for the Earned Wage Access service?
The cost structure varies. In the most common Employer-Integrated Model, the employer contracts with and often pays a subscription fee to the EWA provider. The employee then pays a small transaction fee only when they choose to access their wages instantly. In some cases, the employer covers the transaction fees as an added benefit to the employee.
If I use Pay on Demand, will my final paycheck be smaller?
Yes, absolutely. This is the most important thing to remember. The amount of wages you access early, plus any transaction fees, will be deducted from your final, regular paycheck. For example, if your paycheck is $2,000 and you take a $600 advance, your deposit on payday will be $1,400 minus any transfer fees. Us payroll tax guide wisconsin 2025
Can an employer offer Pay on Demand without a third-party app?
While an employer technically could process early wage requests manually, it creates a massive administrative burden, increases the risk of payroll errors, and can complicate compliance. The entire value of “Pay on Demand” comes from the seamless, automated integration provided by a third-party technology platform, which handles the real-time tracking, disbursement, and deduction without the payroll team having to do extra work.
What types of businesses are adopting Pay on Demand the most?
The trend is strong across the board, but industries with high turnover rates and a large percentage of hourly or shift workers are leading the charge. This includes Retail and E-commerce, which holds the top industry position with a 21% market share, as well as hospitality and healthcare. Large enterprises 59.7% of the market are also big adopters as a key employee retention tool.
How quickly can I get my money with EWA?
If you opt for the instant transfer option, you can typically receive your funds within minutes. This option usually involves a small flat fee. If you choose the free option, the funds are typically deposited via ACH within 1 to 3 business days.
How does Pay on Demand handle tax deductions and withholdings?
Your tax deductions and withholdings are not taken out when you access your wages early. The EWA advance is an advance on your gross earnings. Your employer is still legally responsible for calculating and withholding all necessary federal, state, and local taxes, as well as any other deductions like benefits, from your full gross paycheck amount on the scheduled payday. This is why your final, net paycheck on payday will be smaller than the gross amount minus the advance.

Fintech-powered earned wage access (EWA) has been gathering momentum for nearly a decade, enabling cash-strapped workers to receive a portion of their wages before the usual biweekly payday through digital channels. In that time, EWA has become a hotbed of innovation as fintechs continue to increase the speed and convenience of receiving funds.
But EWA products are also generating controversy, with consumer advocates claiming frequent usage of certain fee-based EWA services can cost almost as much as a
Many fintechs work directly with payroll firms or employers — Walmart is one example — to offer EWA services for free. Others charge a fee ranging from about $1.99 to about $4.99 for each wage-advancement. A handful of other fintechs market EWA products directly to consumers, a practice that consumer advocates fear could lead to misuse due to providers' inability to directly verify participants' income.
Recent data from Sapient Insights Group suggests at least 13% of employers offer earned wage access to workers, and about 30% are planning to do so, as consumer demand for immediate wages rises.
"New technologies such as faster payments, real-time updates and digital accounts can help people manage their money with minimal disruption, and these technological advances are helping EWA users," said Brian Tate, CEO and president of the Innovative Payments Association, a trade group based in Washington, D.C. Last week, the organization launched a website, EarnedWageAccess.info, to raise awareness of the expanding industry.

Earned wage access platforms (EWA) are digital financial tools that allow people to access their earned wages before payday. They offer users an alternative to traditional methods of accessing their income, such as waiting until the end of the pay period or relying on overdrafts and short-term loans. EWA platforms are becoming increasingly popular with employers and employees alike, as they provide a quick, convenient way to access funds when needed.
At its core, an EWA platform is essentially a form of paycheck advance. Through these platforms, employers can make salary advances available to their employees. The employee then has the option to receive the funds immediately or wait until payday. This method gives workers access to money they’ve already earned without waiting for payday and affords them more control over their own finances which can be especially beneficial for those living paycheck-to-paycheck. For employers, offering EWA also reduces overhead costs associated with administering traditional payroll systems like direct deposits and paper checks.
The way it works differs from platform to platform but generally speaking, most services will draw from two sources: employer contributions and/or third-party partners who provide financial products such as lines of credit or prepaid cards. Employers will often contribute by making an upfront payment equal to all or some portion of the employee’s salary into an account linked with the EWA platform and automated on a certain schedule (e.g., biweekly). Third-party partners may also play a role in providing additional funding support via lines of credit or simply paying out cash advances when needed by employees.
EWA providers typically charge fees for their services depending on how much money is accessed early as well as other factors such as transaction volume, average balance, etc. Most charge single flat fees per transaction although some providers may choose to waive these fees altogether if certain requirements are met (such as minimum usage). In addition, there could be fees associated with late payments, bounced checks, etc. These fees should be outlined clearly up front so that users know exactly what they’re getting into before signing up for the service.
One of the most prominent benefits associated with EWA is improved financial health amongst those utilizing it – studies have shown that individuals who use these types of platforms tend to have fewer overdrafts and late payments than those who don’t which in turn leads to improved credit scores over time. As mentioned earlier this type of technology also offers employers numerous advantages including cost savings due to eliminating extra paperwork or processing times associated with traditional payroll approaches while at the same time providing flexibility for workers in terms of when they receive their wages.
Overall Earned Wage Access Platforms provide a much-needed solution in today's gig economy allowing companies large & small alike an opportunity to offer fair & flexible compensation solutions while at the same time helping alleviate any financial stress felt by employees waiting for their next paychecks.
- Financial Inclusion: Earned Wage Access (EWA) platforms give workers the opportunity to manage their finances in real-time, allowing them to access the wages they have already earned on demand. This increases financial inclusion by providing an additional source of income when needed, reducing reliance on traditional lenders who often charge high-interest rates or fees.
- Improved cash flow: Companies that offer EWA can benefit from improved cash flow as their employees will be able to pay for goods and services immediately which will reduce the need for costly credit lines.
- Employee Retention: Employees who have access to their wages at any time are more likely to remain with an employer because they are not solely relying on payday as an incentive or being limited by how much they can save up until then.
- Happier Employees: Helping employees better manage their finances can lead to greater job satisfaction, fewer absences due to financial-related stress, and increased productivity in the workplace.
- Cost Savings: By choosing an EWA platform, businesses avoid incurring larger costs associated with payroll administration and issuing physical checks or direct deposits which could take days or weeks depending on when payday falls within your payroll cycle.
Earned wage access (EWA) platforms are becoming increasingly important as they provide a financial lifeline to people who may not have the same advantages or privileges as those with traditional banking accounts. Without EWA platforms, these individuals would be forced to rely upon paycheck-to-paycheck living, high cost payday loans, or other predatory financial products. EWA platforms offer a more responsible way to manage money and oftentimes can help consumers to budget better and avoid costly fees associated with over-drafting their bank account.
Earning wages is essential for nearly all Americans; often it represents the primary source of income for low-income working households. For countless workers across the U.S., having reliable access to earned wages is fundamental for everyday expenses like rent, childcare payments, gas for the car, groceries etc.; however many employers don’t pay in real time which leads to employees suffer from delayed payment problems that can be financially debilitating.
Fortunately, there are now modern solutions available by way of EWA platforms that allow employees instant access to their hard-earned wages so they can pay bills immediately while avoiding late fees and additional debt due to heavy interest rates of loan products such as payday loans, etc. By giving people greater control over how they use their earnings in real-time through such services, helps bridge gaps in existing banking infrastructures and encourages positive financial behaviors amongst users. In addition, it puts into motion trends that could eventually lead towards improved economic mobility by providing a platform outside of conventional banks or credit unions that opens up new avenues of wealth-building opportunities otherwise denied to them because of lack of credit score or history, etc.
Ultimately earned wage access platforms are an invaluable tool for those looking for greater financial control over their day-to-day lives without being subjected to overly burdensome fees found within traditional forms of finance; helping create a sense of stability and independence that many take for granted yet millions still struggle without every day.
- Direct Deposit: Earned wage access platforms often provide direct deposit of wages, allowing employees to have their payroll disbursed immediately, rather than waiting a few days until the next paycheck date. This feature is especially helpful for employees who need access to their wages quickly.
- Automated Payments: With an earned wage access platform, businesses can automate all payroll transactions for each pay period in order to streamline the process and ensure accurate payments are made on time. This includes setting up recurring payments as well as one-time payments for bonuses and commissions.
- Flexible Payment Schedules: Employees can customize their payment schedules with some earned wage access apps; this means they can choose when they want their wages deposited into their bank accounts and whether or not they want to receive the full amount of the paycheck at once or in installments over a set timeframe (e.g., weekly or biweekly).
- Budgeting Tools: Many platforms include budgeting tools so that individuals can monitor spending and ensure they are being financially responsible with their earnings, safely saving money when possible rather than frivolously using a sudden influx of cash received from a payday deposit. Additionally, some apps offer features that allow workers to break down expenses into categories such as rent/utilities, groceries, entertainment, etc., making it easier to track monthly budgets more effectively.
- Mobile Accessibility: To make earning wages even more accessible and convenient, many earned wage access platforms boast mobile apps that make accessing funds even simpler through smartphones or tablets—making it easy for people to stay on top of their finances on the go from anywhere in the world.
- Low Wage Workers - Those in the lower wage bracket who often struggle to make ends meet financially may benefit from using an earned wage access platform. These workers are often paid hourly and don’t have the same financial stability higher-wage earners have, so having immediate access to their wages can provide a much-needed boost.
- Gig Workers - This growing workforce is composed of individuals who work in a contract-based way with no steady income or benefits as part of their employment agreement. They often rely on sporadic paychecks and may find themselves needing quick cash; an earned wage access platform could help them draw small amounts of money at any time without impacting their savings goals.
- Freelancers - People who work for themselves or offer services are usually paid on a per-project basis which means payment cycles can be unpredictable—they might feel strapped for funds between projects and turn to an earned wage access platform for short-term solutions.
- Small Business Owners - While many traditional employers now use platforms like this, entrepreneurs may also find it useful if they’re not able to cover immediate expenses immediately but want to avoid taking out loans or dipping into long-term savings plans. Instead, they can leverage the money already owed to them through employee wages when necessary.
- Unbanked Individuals – Those without bank accounts typically have limited options when it comes to accessing funds quickly, but with an earned wage access platform, they’ll be able to get paid instantly without having an account set up elsewhere first.
The cost of using earned wage access platforms depends on the platform that you choose and the individual features offered by each platform. Generally, there are no set-up fees with most earned wage access platforms, but there may be monthly subscription fees or transaction fees applied. Typically, these fees range from 1-5% of a transaction depending on the platform. Additionally, some platforms may charge for other services such as payroll or data integration. It's important to do your research and compare different provider prices when selecting an earned wage access platform in order to ensure you find a plan that works best for your company’s needs.
- Liquidity Risk: Earned wage access platforms rely on employers to provide payouts, but if the employer lacks sufficient funds or fails to make a timely payment, employees may be unable to access their wages in a timely manner.
- Security Risk: There is also the potential risk of security breaches or hacking which could compromise employee data and potentially lead to identity theft and other financial losses.
- Compliance Risk: Earned wage access platforms must comply with applicable laws, including those related to taxation, payroll deductions, and labor laws. If these laws are not followed, employers and employees may face penalties or fines.
- Interest Rate Risks: Another risk associated with earned wage access platforms is that some providers will charge high interest rates on advances or late payments which can be financially burdensome for employees.
- Reputation Risk: Finally, any negative publicity surrounding earned wage access platforms can have a detrimental impact on an employer’s reputation and could reduce customer trust in their services.
Earned wage access platforms can integrate with a variety of different software types, including payroll and human resource management systems (HRMS), accounting applications, enterprise resource planning (ERP) systems, customer relationship management (CRM) solutions, web portals, time tracking tools, financial planning services and blockchain-based applications. This enables the platform to seamlessly access employee data from those sources in order to accurately approve early payments in near real-time at minimal incremental cost. Additionally, some providers offer APIs for developers to build custom integrations that give employers the flexibility needed to tailor their earned wage access solution to fit their unique requirements.

questions.question_text: What are good day trips from Los Angeles?

documents.text:
Los Angeles, CA is a city known for its entertainment, beaches, and nightlife. While there are many activities to do in the City of Angels, you may have the urge to escape the city borders to explore something new. There are many unique day trips you can take – whether a longer trip to a national park or a shorter trip to an amusement park. Any of which are sure to pique your interest. To help you get started, we compiled a list of the 10 best day trips from Los Angeles. Keep reading to see what trips made the list.
1. Coronado, CA
Approximate distance: 130 miles
Estimated travel time: 3 hours
Just 3 hours and 130 miles south of Los Angeles lies Coronado, CA, a beautiful resort city located across the Big Bay from downtown San Diego, CA. Coronado, a name derived from the Coronado Islands, bears the nickname, “The Crown City.” There are many activities to do in Coronado such as visiting the USS Midway Museum, lounging at Coronado Beach, or going boating along the bay. If you find yourself wanting to stay for the weekend, book a room at the Hotel del Coronado, the second largest wooden structure in the United States.
2. Joshua Tree National Park
Approximate distance: 130 miles
Estimated travel time: 3 hours
Known for its distinct plants and starry nights, there is no shortage of adventure at Joshua Tree National Park. The park comprises two desert ecosystems, the Mojave and Colorado, and encompasses about 790,000 acres making it the second-largest national park in California, second only to Death Valley National Park. There are many things to do at Joshua Tree such as trying out the various climbing routes, hiking the many trails like the Arch Rock Nature Trail and Ryan Mountain Trail; or taking in the views at Barker Dam. It takes approximately 3 hours to get to Joshua Tree National Park so make sure to wake up early for this day trip from Los Angeles.
3. San Diego, CA
Approximate distance: 120 miles
Estimated travel time: 3 hours
If you are looking for some fun and excitement take a trip to San Diego, CA. Located roughly 3 hours east of Los Angeles, San Diego, CA is known as, “America’s Finest City” with its beautiful beaches and wonderful weather. The city lies along the Pacific Ocean and has unique typography filled with canyons, valleys, and mesas. If you head out to San Diego, be sure to explore the San Diego Zoo where you can see more than 650 species; Balboa Park, a historic cultural park with gardens, open spaces, and walking trails; and La Jolla Cove, a beautiful beach with surrounding cliffs.
4. San Gabriel Mountains National Monument
Approximate distance: 50 miles
Estimated travel time: 2 hours
San Gabriel Mountains National Monument spans over 340,000 miles and holds 600 archeological sites. It’s comprised of four different wilderness areas – San Gabriel, Sheep Mountain, Magic Mountain, and Pleasant View Ridge. San Gabriel Mountains National Monument is located about 2 hours and 50 miles east of Los Angeles making it a quick day trip from this city. When at San Gabriel Mountains National Monument you can do many different outdoor activities like hiking, cross-country skiing, and hunting.
5. Palm Springs, CA
Approximate distance: 100 miles
Estimated travel time: 1 hour and 50 minutes
If you are looking for fun in the sun consider checking out Palm Springs, CA. Palm Springs is considered the golf capital of the world and is located about 100 miles east of Los Angeles. You can get to Palm Springs, CA in about 1 hour and 50 minutes. A couple of activities to try out include golfing at Pete Dye Mountain Course, Desert Willow, or Escena Golf Club; watching tennis at the BNP Paribas Open, or exploring the Living Desert Zoo and Garden. With the diversity of activities, it’s no wonder why Palm Springs is considered one of the best day trips from Los Angeles.
6. Santa Catalina Island
Approximate distance: 50 miles
Estimated travel time: 1 hour
Located nearly 50 miles West of Los Angeles, Santa Catalina Island lies just off the Pacific Coast of California and is a favorite destination for boaters, adventurers, and tourists alike. A couple of activities to try out in Santa Catalina include lounging at Moonstone Beach, taking a tour of Avalon Theater, or visiting Catalina Museum for Art & History. Make sure to account for around one hour boat ride to Santa Catalina Island.
7. Tijuana, MX
Approximate distance: 220 miles
Estimated travel time: 3.5 hours
Located about 3 hours and 30 minutes from Los Angeles, the town of Tijuana, MX is known for its bullfighting and racetracks. In fact, Tijuana has one of the only seaside bullrings in the world, only second in size to Plaza México. Some things to check out in Tijuana include picking produce at the El Popo Market, checking out Avenida Revolucion, or walking along Tijuana’s scenic beaches.
8. Big Bear Lake
Approximate distance: 120 miles
Estimated travel time: 3 hours
Around 3 hours and 120 miles east of Los Angeles, Big Bear Lake, CA provides access to a ton of outdoor activities such as skiing, hiking, paddleboarding, and jet skiing. The city sits along a large fish-filled lake and is surrounded by beautiful pine trees of the San Bernardino National Forest. Many people go to Big Bear Lake to go skiing at Bear Mountain Ski Resort, visit animals at Big Bear Alpine Zoo, or hike Castle Rock trail. For an unforgettable experience, try to visit one of the many year-round events held at Big Bear like the Fishing for 50k Trout Derby or Big Bear Lake Oktoberfest.
9. Disneyland
Approximate distance: 30 miles
Estimated travel time: 30 minutes
If you want to try delicious food, love entertaining shows, or want to experience magic, this day trip is for you. Known as The Happiest Place of Earth, Disneyland is roughly 30 miles southeast of Los Angeles located in Anaheim, CA. Disneyland is full of fun activities for people of all ages. You can take pictures in front of the Magic Castle, ride Space Mountain, and travel up the Matterhorn. Make sure to wake up early for this day trip from Los Angeles as crowds can fill up quickly, especially during the weekends.
10. Solvang, CA
Approximate distance: 130 miles
Estimated travel time: 2 hours
If the idea of shopping at small businesses, going wine sampling, or strolling through a village sounds fun to you, then take a day trip to Solvang, CA. Situated 130 miles and nearly 2 hours northwest of Los Angeles, Solvang, CA is a historic Danish town that you’ll never get bored exploring. Some favorite things to see are the Little Mermaid statue and the historic church of Old Mission Santa Ines. You can also visit the town during an annual event like Solvang Stomp held in October or Danish Days held in September.

Los Angeles is already one of those places everyone’s heard about. But what really makes LA extra fun are all the tours and easy day trips you can add to your plans. There’s always a new corner to check out in the city or a quick escape just outside of it. That’s what makes exploring LA feel like a new adventure every time. Here, I’ve made a list of all the top tours and day trips you can take while in LA.
In a Hurry? Here Are Our Top 4 Los Angeles Tours and Day Trips Picks
Before We Escape…
While you most definitely can let your inner, spontaneous adventurer self out, taking trips are supposed to be relaxing (unless, you want the adrenaline rush of traveling unprepared, because kudos to you then). I highly recommend booking the things you need to book in advance. This includes tickets and admission fees.
You can also join organized day trips for a more relaxed experience. Some of the tours offer multiple stops that I recommend here, so it’ll be killing two, or more, birds with one stone.
Warner Bros. Studio Tour Hollywood
Best For: Behind-the-scenes movie magic, set tours, classic TV nostalgia
If you’re curious about how movies and TV shows come to life, I think the Warner Bros. Studio Tour is a must-do day trip while you’re in Los Angeles. It’s one of the best ways to get an insider’s look at real working sets, soundstages, and iconic filming locations. Located in Burbank, it’s about 20 minutes from central LA by car, so it’s super easy to fit into your itinerary.
One highlight is the Studio Tour itself. You’ll ride around the backlots where countless films and series have been shot, from classics like Friends to modern hits like The Big Bang Theory and Gilmore Girls. I also recommend spending time at Stage 48: Script to Screen, an interactive exhibit where you can sit on the famous Central Perk couch, see real costumes, and learn how a show is made from start to finish. If you’re a superhero fan, then definitely check out the DC Universe exhibit and the Batmobiles collection. And for Harry Potter fans, you can even get “sorted” into your Hogwarts House.
Getting There: A Classic Hollywood Tour in Los Angeles
It’s easy to visit Warner Bros. Studio on your own. Just book your Warner Bros. Studio Tour Hollywood tickets online in advance to secure your spot. You’ll join a small group and a guide to explore legendary backlots, soundstages, the famous Central Perk café, and behind-the-scenes movie magic.
The studio is in Burbank, about 20 minutes from central LA by car, with on-site parking available for a fee.
Quick Tips
- Book your studio tour tickets ahead of time. Popular time slots can sell out, especially on weekends and during holiday seasons.
- Bring a valid photo ID; you’ll need it to enter the studio.
- Large bags and filming on the tour are not allowed, but you can take photos at designated spots.
Santa Catalina Island
Best For: Island adventure, ocean views, laid-back coastal charm
Travel Time: ~2 hours from Los Angeles (including the ferry)
Just a short hop from LA, Catalina Island is like a whole new world. I think it’s one of the best day trips if you want to swap city streets for turquoise water and breezy island vibes. Catalina mixes SoCal cool with a touch of the Mediterranean, making it perfect for kayaking, snorkeling, or just soaking up Avalon’s harbor charm.
Out on the water, you can paddle through sea caves, snorkel in clear coves, or spot dolphins right from the ferry. Back on land, golf carts are the fun way to explore Avalon’s streets, hidden corners, and famous spots like the Catalina Casino. And if you’re a foodie, Catalina’s local bites are worth the trip alone. You can enjoy fresh seafood, sweets, and island history in one tasty stroll.
Getting There: A Coastal Day Trip from Los Angeles
Catalina is easy to reach. Just drive or rideshare to Long Beach and catch the Catalina Express ferry (this one’s from San Pedro to Avalon). Most people reach Avalon in about an hour once they’re onboard. I recommend booking tickets early, especially in summer or on weekends.
Once you’re there, there are some great ways to see the island. Out on the water, kayaking through sea caves is a must. Or you can stay dry but still see under the waves; I really recommend the Yellow Semi-Submarine tour. It’s quick, fun, and lets you watch schools of fish without getting wet.
Back in Avalon, golf carts are the way to explore. For the easiest adventure, I suggest booking this private guided golf cart tour. You’ll roll past the Catalina Casino, Pebbly Beach, and Wrigley Memorial with local stories along the way.
And if you’re craving local flavor, a food tour is the way to go. Taking a Catalina food tour is a tasty stroll along the waterfront with fresh seafood, sweets, and island history mixed in.
Quick Tips
- Bring layers. The ocean breeze can surprise you!
- Pack reef-safe sunscreen if you plan to snorkel or kayak.
- If you want to see dolphins, grab a seat on the ferry’s top deck for the best chance.
Joshua Tree National Park
Best For: Surreal desert scenery, rock formations, and stargazing
Travel Time: ~2.5–3 hours from Los Angeles
Just about 130 miles southeast of Los Angeles, Joshua Tree National Park is one of the best ways to trade city traffic for wide-open desert skies. I think it’s the perfect pick if you want to see a desert with strange, beautiful views: spiky Joshua trees, giant boulders, and sunsets that glow over the rocks.
The park’s otherworldly scenery is a dream for photographers and rock climbers alike. Even if you’re not into climbing cliffs, there are plenty of giant rock piles you can scramble up for fun and panoramic views. I suggest the Hidden Valley Trail for an easy, family-friendly 1-mile loop that shows off classic Joshua Tree sights. For more adventure, the 49 Palms Oasis Trail is a 3-mile trek to a surprise palm oasis tucked in the middle of the desert.
Getting There: A Desert Day Trip from Los Angeles
Start your adventure by either driving yourself or booking a tour that picks you up right from your hotel. It’s about a 2.5–3 hour drive from Los Angeles, so it’s totally doable as a day trip if you plan ahead.
If you’d rather not navigate on your own, I suggest this Joshua Tree National Park scenic tour. You’ll ride in a comfy van or an open-air Hummer with a small group and a guide who knows all the best viewpoints and geology stories. It’s perfect for families or first-time visitors who want an easy half-day escape.
For those who want to go at their own pace, try this self-guided driving audio tour. It follows a curated route with fun facts and hidden highlights along the way, plus a bonus stop at the Hidden Valley Nature Trail.
For adventure lovers, I recommend an off-road 4×4 tour that takes you deep into Joshua Tree’s rugged backcountry and lesser-seen valleys. Or you can try the open-air Hummer adventure, which adds a bit of thrill while you explore desert oases, spot wildlife, and snap photos of dramatic rock formations.
Quick Tips
- The drive takes approximately 2 hours and 45 minutes from LA, but plan for a full day (or longer) to truly appreciate what the park offers.
- Arrive early to beat both crowds and desert heat, especially during summer months.
Iconic Sights of Los Angeles Tour
Best For: First-timers, city highlights, classic LA photo ops
Travel Time: Full-day city tour (approx. 7–8 hours)
If you want to see all the highlights that make LA special in just one day, I think this full-day tour is a great choice. You’ll visit Hollywood’s Walk of Fame, the legendary Sunset Strip, the palm-lined streets of Beverly Hills, and the relaxed beaches around Santa Monica without the stress of planning every stop yourself.
Then, you can snap a photo at the Hollywood Sign, wander along Rodeo Drive, and soak up the ocean breeze at Venice Beach or the Santa Monica Pier. If you’re short on time, grouping a few highlights in one day is a fun way to get a good feel for what makes the city so iconic.
Getting There: A Must-Do City Tour in Los Angeles
Seeing LA’s biggest highlights can be tricky if you’re short on time. So, I recommend this full-day tour of the iconic sights of Los Angeles to make it easy. I really recommend it if you want to check off Hollywood, Beverly Hills, the Sunset Strip, Venice Beach, and Santa Monica Pier all in one day without the stress of driving or parking.
If you’re really tight on time, there’s also a half-day tour available. You’ll ride in an air-conditioned mini coach with a live guide, stop at top spots like the Hollywood Sign, Griffith Observatory, and Santa Monica Pier, and enjoy fun insider gossip along the way, plus audio guides in 11 languages if you depart from Hollywood.
Or, for the ultimate overview, I recommend the Grand City Tour of Los Angeles, Hollywood and Beverly Hills. It’s perfect if you want a comprehensive look at LA in one trip, with convenient hotel pickup, drop-off, and free time for lunch or shopping in between iconic stops.
Quick Tips
- Charge your phone. You’ll want it ready for snapping photos at all the famous spots, plus you might need maps or rideshare apps afterward.
- Plan for traffic. Even on a guided tour, LA traffic is real. Bring water, snacks, and something to keep you entertained while you’re on the road.
Malibu
Best For: Coastal road trips, iconic beaches, oceanfront dining
Travel Time: ~45 minutes from downtown Los Angeles (33 miles)
Just under an hour from LA, Malibu is a classic day trip when you want ocean views and beach vibes without going far. The Pacific Coast Highway alone is worth the drive. There are dramatic cliffs, hidden coves, and photo stops at every turn.
Malibu’s beaches are some of SoCal’s best. I recommend El Matador for sea caves and sunset shots, Zuma for wide open sand and swimming, and Malibu Lagoon for surf culture and celeb spotting. If you have extra time, hike scenic canyon trails, browse the Malibu Country Mart, or grab tacos and picnic right on the sand.
Getting There: A Seaside Day Trip from Los Angeles
Malibu is one of the easiest and most rewarding escapes from LA. Just jump on the Pacific Coast Highway and head west. In about 45 minutes, you’ll get ocean cliffs, beach pull-offs, and breezy coastal views make the drive part of the adventure.
If you’d rather let someone else handle the driving, you’ve got some great ways to explore. One good option is the Malibu: Exclusive Beautiful Beach and Celebrity Lifestyle Tour. You’ll ride in an open-air van, take in stories about Malibu’s celebrity history, and stop at classic spots like Malibu Pier, Point Dume’s ocean cliffs, and the Adamson House. You’ll also have time to browse the Malibu Country Mart for a snack or a quick shop.
For something more laid-back, this private vintage VW bus tour is a fun twist! It mixes local wine tasting with a mellow cruise through Malibu’s canyons and coastal roads. It’s definitely a relaxed way to see hidden lookouts and maybe spot some local wildlife along the way.
If you want to stretch your legs, I recommend the guided vineyard hike. It’s an easy loop through Malibu’s rolling hills with stops for local history and even a look at Chumash cave paintings. It wraps up with a couple cans of local wine to enjoy after your walk, which is a nice way to combine a bit of nature with something to sip.
Or, if you’re up for a bit of everything, try this Malibu Wine, Food & Beach Tour. It covers scenic roads, tucked-away nature preserves, and a stop at a private beach for photos. You’ll ride in an open-air bus with snacks and wine on board.
Quick Tips
- Leave early. The Pacific Coast Highway is beautiful but can get busy fast, especially on weekends.
- Bring layers and sunscreen. Pack a light jacket and plenty of sunblock.
Hollywood
Best For: Movie magic, famous landmarks, pop culture history
Travel Time: Right in the heart of Los Angeles
While Hollywood pops up in most city tours, this spotlight trip is all about soaking in everything that makes Tinseltown iconic. Hollywood is where LA’s movie magic really comes alive.
You can spend your day tracing the footsteps of legends at the TCL Chinese Theatre, hunting for your favorite stars on the boulevard, or even catching a glimpse of the Hollywood Sign perched above it all. If you love old-school glamour mixed with pop culture, a deep dive into Hollywood’s streets, studios, and behind-the-scenes stories is a must while you’re in LA.
Getting There: A Star-Studded Hollywood Tour in Los Angeles
One of the best things about exploring Hollywood is that you’re already in LA so no long drive is needed. Once you’re there, you can easily hop on a sightseeing tour or set out on foot to soak up the neighborhood’s most iconic spots.
For a fun overview without the parking headaches, I think an open-air bus is the way to go. The Hollywood open bus tours cruise past all the classics like the Walk of Fame, Dolby Theatre, Rodeo Drive, and those famous movie star homes you’ve always heard about. If you’d like a mix of Beverly Hills mansions and Hollywood landmarks, there’s also this Hollywood and Celebrity Homes Bus Tour hits the highlights and keeps an eye out for celebrity sightings too. There’s also the same tour plus Beverly Hills, but this time on an open air bus.
But if you’d rather explore on foot (and get closer to that iconic sign), I recommend lacing up for this Hollywood Sign Tour with comedians & their dogs. It is a unique experience! It’s a guided walk through Griffith Park with plenty of laughs, history, and epic skyline views. Or go all in on a classic LA bucket list moment with the original 2.5-Hour Hollywood sign hike, which gets you as close as possible to the sign (and helps you snap those envy-inducing shots without getting lost in the hills).
Quick Tips
- Bring water and sunscreen if you’re doing a hike. Griffith Park gets hot, especially midday.
- Keep cash handy for quick snacks or small souvenirs along Hollywood Boulevard.
- If you’re hoping to spot a celeb, hang out near trendy cafes or head up to the hills. You never know who you’ll see!
Griffith Observatory
Best For: Skyline views, stargazing, classic LA scenery
Travel Time: ~20–30 minutes from downtown Los Angeles
Perched high above the city in Griffith Park, Griffith Observatory is one of LA’s most beloved landmarks for good reason. It’s where locals and visitors alike come to soak up sweeping views of the city skyline, the Hollywood Sign, and the endless SoCal sunsets that make this spot a must.
Once you step inside, check out the free space exhibits, peer through historic telescopes, or catch a live show in the Samuel Oschin Planetarium. If you’re more into fresh air than star charts, the trails around the observatory lead to some of the best lookout points in LA. It’s perfect for snapping skyline photos or just soaking up that classic Southern California sunset.
Getting There: A Breathtaking Tour in Los Angeles
Griffith Observatory is just a quick drive from downtown Los Angeles, but part of the fun is getting there, especially if you love a good view along the way. Parking at the top can get tight on busy days, so a lot of visitors combine their trip with a scenic hike through Griffith Park instead.
One of the best ways to do it is on a guided walk, like this guided hiking tour through Griffith Park up towards the observatory. You’ll follow an expert local guide along a 3.5-mile route through the Hollywood Hills, learn fun bits of LA history, and get those must-have photos of the Hollywood Sign. The hike ends right at the Observatory, so you can explore inside or just relax and take in the sweeping skyline views. Morning and sunset departures mean you can pick your favorite vibe, be it golden light or city lights!
Quick Tips
- Bring a light jacket as it can get breezy up at the Observatory, especially after sunset.
- The planetarium shows aren’t free. Check the schedule and grab tickets early if you want to catch one.
- Stay after dark if you can! Telescopes on the lawn offer free public viewing on clear nights.
Big Bear Lake
Best For: Mountain escapes, fresh alpine air, year-round outdoor fun
Travel Time: ~2 hours from downtown Los Angeles
Just two hours from the bustle of Los Angeles, Big Bear Lake sits high in the San Bernardino Mountains at over 6,700 feet. This alpine village feels like a world away, with cool mountain breezes and pine forests that offer a refreshing break from the city’s heat.
Big Bear is fun to visit any time of year. In summer, rent a boat and spend time on the water. When spring arrives, the hills bloom with colorful wildflowers. Fall brings bright leaves and crisp air, while winter turns the area into a snowy playground for skiing and snow fun. Even though it’s so close to the city, it has completely different vibes that you will like if you’ve had enough of the bustle of LA.
Getting There: A Scenic Mountain Day Trip from Los Angeles
Reaching Big Bear Lake from Los Angeles is pretty straightforward. Most visitors take Highway 330 or Highway 18, winding through scenic mountain roads with sweeping views of the San Bernardino National Forest. It’s about a two-hour drive, but plan extra time to stop at overlooks or snap photos along the way.
Once you’re up there, you don’t have to stick to the usual trails or crowded spots. For something fun and local-approved, I recommend trying this locals’ favorite hike with lake swimming experience. You’ll get a short guided hike through the forest and then cool off at a secret swimming dock. It’s really the kind of hidden perk you’d only find with a local.
Or if you’d rather keep things laid-back, you can combine the mountain views with a little gourmet twist on the with this Big Bear Lake jeep tour with light lunch. It’s part scenic ride, part storytelling session, and ends with a stylish pop-up picnic in a forest spot known mostly to locals. It’s perfect for a quiet lunch surrounded by fresh mountain air.
Quick Tips
- Check the weather. It can change fast in the mountains.
- Fill up on gas early. There aren’t many gas stations up in Big Bear, so top off before you start driving up the mountain roads.
- Take it slow on the roads. The mountain highways are beautiful but winding. Drive carefully and enjoy the views along the way.
More Fun Little Adventures Around Los Angeles
Echo Park Swan Boats
If you feel like swapping the city noise for something chill, I think paddling a swan boat around Echo Park Lake is a cute idea. It’s easy, affordable, and you can pick daytime or even go at night when the skyline’s all lit up. Nice way to just float, talk, and enjoy a break.
Ultimate LA Bike Tour
For something more active, you might like this full-day bike ride through West Hollywood, Beverly Hills, Santa Monica, and Venice. I like that it mixes cycling with little stories, celeb house sightings, and a stop at Greystone Mansion. It’s a fun way to cover a lot of ground without feeling rushed.
Universal Studios Hollywood: VIP Tour
If you’re into theme parks but hate standing in line all day, this VIP Universal pass could be worth it. You skip the lines, get a behind-the-scenes peek at real movie sets, and there’s even valet parking and a good meal thrown in. Not bad if you want to make the most of your day there.
Your Perfect LA Escape Awaits
Before you head out, keep a few things in mind to make the most of your LA day trips. Always check the weather, pack layers and sunscreen, and wear comfy shoes since you might hit a beach, a canyon, and a city street all in one day. If you’re driving, plan for traffic and parking fees, and start early when you can to avoid crowds.
It’s also worth keeping your energy up with some local bites. LA’s food scene is too good to skip! If you need ideas, I suggest browsing these famous Los Angeles foods for must-try eats along the way. And if you’re still building your plan, this list of things to do in Los Angeles can help round out your adventures. Enjoy exploring!

Introduction
I woke up in my tiny Koreatown apartment, craving ocean air that didn’t smell like taco grease and Uber exhaust. By 7:15 a.m. I had a mug of cheap coffee, a half-charged phone, and enough gas to get somewhere—anywhere—before the 405 turned into a parking lot. These five day trips from los angeles saved my sanity over the past year; each one fits into a single Saturday, costs less than a Disneyland churro stand, and gives you bragging rights that don’t involve filtering selfies at the Hollywood sign.
Santa Barbara: ninety minutes to fake European bliss
The 101 north is a straight shot, but I still manage to miss the exit every time. Roll down the windows around Ventura and the air turns salty; by the time you hit Santa Barbara the temperature drops five degrees and your playlist suddenly feels more sophisticated. Park at East Beach lot ($2.25 per hour, card accepted) and walk the palm-lined path toward Stearns Wharf. I once saw a pelican steal a toddler’s sandwich here—equal parts horrifying and hilarious.
Almond croissants and hidden courtyards
I follow the same route each visit: croissant at Renaud’s (still warm, flaky enough to ruin your shirt), then a wander up State Street until the tilework of the old courthouse appears. If you’re building a bucket-list of single-day escapes, my Top Bucket List Travel Destinations You Can Explore in a Single Day guide rounds up global spots you can steal. I follow the same route each visit: croissant at Renaud’s (still warm, flaky enough to ruin your shirt), then a wander up State Street until the tilework of the old courthouse appears. Climb the tower—free, no line—and you’ll see red-tile roofs crammed between mountains and sea. Later I cut over to Anapamu Street, duck into the public library’s back garden, and pretend I’m in a Spanish novella for twenty minutes. No tour bus stops here; that’s the point.
Cheap wine without the side-eye
Santa Barbara’s Urban Wine Trail sounds bougie until you realize most tasting rooms pour for $10 and waive the fee if you buy a bottle. My go-to is Riverbench on Anacapa; their sparkling rosé tastes like strawberry Pop Rocks and the bartender lets you keep the glass. Dump the guilt, stash the glass in your trunk, and you’re back on the 101 before sunset traffic spawns.
Joshua Tree: where your phone gives up and you remember what stars look like
Two hours east and the city dissolves into wind farms, then boulder fields that feel like a Dr. Seuss fever dream. I always stop at the Joshua Tree Visitor Center for a map—even though the loop roads are basically a figure eight—because the ranger behind the counter gives free coffee refills to anyone carrying a reusable cup. If you ever flip the map to the desert north-east, my Unforgettable Day Trips from Las Vegas guide covers sun-to-snow routes in the same timeframe. Pro tip: bring the cup.
Hidden Valley loop before the crowds
I hit Hidden Valley Trail at sunrise; the parking lot has three cars max and the rocks glow pink. The loop is only one mile, but you’ll spend forty minutes photographing cacti and trying not to step on lizards. I once watched a guy propose here—she said yes, then immediately asked if there was cell service. (There isn’t.)
Keys View for the price of nothing
Drive another twenty minutes up the ridge and you’ll stare down the Coachella Valley from 5,185 feet. On clear winter days you can see the Salton Sea shimmering like a broken mirror. I sat on the stone wall until my fingers went numb, listening to nothing but wind and the occasional raven. That’s the real luxury—silence you don’t have to pay for.
Date shakes and gas-station art
Leave the park through the west entrance, pull into the funky strip of cabins that calls itself Joshua Tree town. Crossroads Café serves a date shake thick enough to stand a straw upright; I always add a shot of espresso because caffeine in the desert feels poetic. Next door, the thrift store has a wall of VHS tapes for a dollar each—buy one, even if you don’t own a VCR. It’s a souvenir that weighs nothing and sparks conversations.
Malibu: forty-five minutes to feel like a celebrity on a budget
Take the PCH north past Topanga and the cliffs drop into the ocean so fast your ears pop. I usually exit at Las Flores Canyon, park for free along the shoulder, and hike the paved path down to El Matador State Beach. The descent is steep enough to make your calves hate you, but the sea arches at the bottom photograph like a Greek island—no filter, no crowds before 10 a.m.
Sea caves and wet sneakers
Time the tide right (check the chart online) and you can duck into a cave that opens onto a hidden pocket of sand. I once found a message in a plastic bottle here: a kid’s drawing of a dinosaur and the words “be happy.” I left it there; the next person deserves the smile too.
Neptune’s Net: biker bar, surfer cafeteria, your lunch
Cross back over the highway and you’ll hit Neptune’s Net, all neon beer signs and Harley exhaust. Order the clam chowder bread bowl; it’s $12, tastes like salt and nostalgia, and the cashier doesn’t care if you show up in flip-flops or Ferragamo. Sit on the upper deck, watch the Pacific glitter, and try to count how many different languages you hear. I stopped at seven. Prefer palm trees to fog? Check my Ultimate San Francisco Day Trips guide for Nor-Cal ocean-to-redwood escapes too.
Big Bear Lake: two-and-a-half hours to fake winter when L.A. is still sweating
Climb the 330 through Running Springs and the temperature drops a degree every mile. I roll the windows down just to smell pine instead of brake dust. By the time the lake appears—frozen edges in January, glassy blue in July—I’ve already forgotten what freeway rage feels like.
Village Rim Trail for the lazy hiker
No skis? No problem. Park at the Discovery Center, grab a free map, and walk the Village Rim Trail. It’s mostly flat, hugs the shoreline, and delivers postcard views without the elevation guilt. I saw a bald eagle here last March; everyone else was taking selfies at the ski resort parking lot.
Coffee that doesn’t taste like campfire
Amangela’s sits above a bike shop that rents fat-tire cycles for snow. Their blueberry cornmeal muffin is the size of a softball and pairs perfectly with a honey-lavender latte. I always grab an extra muffin for the drive down—it’s gone before I hit the first switchback.
Alpine slide and alpine guilt
If you’re visiting summer-through-fall, the Alpine Slide at Magic Mountain is worth the $20. You ride a plastic sled down a concrete chute, wind in your face, lake expanding below. I screamed the entire way; the eight-year-old behind me did not. Humbling.
Solvang – Denmark without the jet-lag (2 hrs north-west)
Exit the 101 at Buellton, follow the smell of fresh waffles, and suddenly you’re in a Hans Christian Andersen pop-up book. Windmills spin, half-timbered houses lean at impossible angles, and every bakery pumps out almond-scented steam. I park on Copenhagen Drive—three free hours if you feed the meter quarters you found under the seat.
Kringle and Viking selfies
Mortensen’s Bakery has a tray of almond kringle that sells out by 11 a.m. I buy one still warm, eat it on the wooden bench outside, and pretend the calories don’t count on vacation days. Across the street, the giant red clog begs for a foot photo—obligatory, embrace the cliché.
Wine tasting that won’t bankrupt you
Walk two blocks south to Presidio Winery—tiny patio, string lights, laid-back bartender who pours four tastes for $8 and waves the fee if you post an Instagram story tagging them. Their sparkling brut is crisp enough to cut through kringle sugar; I left with two cans (yes, cans) because road-trip rules apply.

You don’t need a private jet, a trust fund, or a three-day weekend. You need half a tank of gas, a Spotify playlist that doesn’t suck, and the guts to leave before sunrise. Every spot on this list I’ve done round-trip in under 12 hours, back home in time to shower, order Thai food, and sleep in my own bed. Terrannea Resort
Drive Time: 31 miles from DTLA.
Why We Love It: You don’t need to be an overnight guest to enjoy the gorgeous splendor of this upscale cliffside resort. Sprawled over 102 acres, Terranea is home to a network of walking and hiking trails that snake along the coastline to the rocky shores below (even dogs are allowed!). Non-guests are welcome to explore the grounds—and there are plenty of wide open hills and fields for littles to run around. When you’re hungry, the casual (albeit pricey) Nelson’s restaurant offers upscale bar food with a killer view. There’s also a bakery by the front entrance that sells all sorts of yummy treats the kids will want to devour. Unique day experiences are also available to non-guests, including art classes, archery, stand-up paddleboarding, kayaking, and a private falconry experience.
Insider’s Tip: Stop by the “Falconry Meet and Greet” every Tuesday, Thursday, Friday, and Saturday from 11-11:30 a.m. to meet Terranea’s falconer and learn about how he works with these majestic birds of prey.
100 Terranea Way
Rancho Palos Verdes

Riley’s Farm & Oak Glen
Drive Time: 80 miles from DTLA
Why We Love It: The best time to visit Oak Glen is the fall, when apple season brings hordes of tourists up for a good picking. But the agricultural community of Oak Glen is also home to Riley’s Farm, which not only offers farm activities and U-pick all year long, but also Revolutionary War reenactments, including “Adventures in the Old World” Saturdays, with old-time favorites like archery, tomahawk throwing and corn husk doll-making.

Catalina Island
Drive Time: Boats leave from Long Beach or San Pedro, which is about 25 miles from DTLA
Why We Love It: The boat ride alone is reason enough to cruise over to our nearest island neighbor. The 1-hour crossing is an easy way to spot whales, dolphins, or other sea life—along with a great view of the SoCal coastline. Once you’ve docked, you’ll feel miles away on this little island where bison roam free and zipline tours whisk you over scenic canyons with views of the Pacific. Rent a golf cart to explore the island on your own, or book a jeep tour to see all the off-road splendor the island has to offer.
It’s worth noting that an amazing 88 percent of Catalina Island is still wild and uninhabited, as it was set aside as protected land by the Catalina Island Conservancy. Consequently, the island has more than 62 miles of unspoiled beaches, and the longest publicly accessible stretch of undeveloped coastline left in Southern California.
Related: Your Guide to Visiting Catalina With Kids
Griffith Park
Drive Time: 7 miles from DTLA
Why We Love It: Be a tourist in your own town! Griffith Park has enough to offer that you can spend a whole day exploring its 4,210 acres of land (It’s one of the largest urban wilderness parks in the country!). Littles will love whirling around on the historic carousel (and they’ll equally love knowing that this is the spot Walt Disney reportedly came up with the idea for Disneyland). Tiny stargazers will definitely want to see the Griffith Observatory—especially if you have time to see a show in the Samuel Oschin Planetarium, one of the largest planetarium domes in the world. You can make a hiking day out of it by parking near the Greek Theatre and taking the one-mile trail up to the observatory; or, there’s plenty of parking at the top as well.
While you may not fit this all into a day, Griffith Park is also home to the 133-acre LA Zoo—as well as Travel Town, where kids can walk around historic trains and get a miniature train ride. Prefer to see the park on horseback? Griffith Park’s Equestrian Center (called The Los Angeles Equestrian Center) offers trail rides for all levels.
4730 Crystal Springs Dr.
Los Angeles

Balboa Village
Drive Time: 47 miles from DTLA.
Why We Love It: With its historic Ferris wheel, bustling eateries, and waterfront charm, Balboa Village is a perfect place to spend a family day. There are bike and boat rentals, a nautical museum, and an old-school candy store specializing in nostalgic sweets. If you have time, hop aboard the ferry to Balboa Island—you might even spot a migrating whale on the way over. And don’t miss the Balboa Fun Zone, which is like a pint-sized Santa Monica Pier with far fewer tourists.
Insider Tip: The area is home to the original frozen banana, so don’t leave without enjoying the delicious chocolate-covered treat. Both Dad’s Donut & Bakery Shop and Sugar ‘n Spice claim to be the first purveyors of the dessert on a stick, but the jury’s still out on which spot is the top banana.

Palm Springs Aerial Tramway
Drive Time: 109 miles from DTLA.
Why We Love It: This tram ride feels like a Disneyland ride, only you’re actually going somewhere (besides around and around). Boasting a two-and-a-half mile ascent on a rotating tram car, it’s thrilling enough for kids (and adults) of all ages. And then, of course, there is the destination: Once atop the peak, there are hiking trails to explore, a small history museum, and a restaurant where you can admire the view and grab a bite to eat at Forest View Restaurant—8500 feet above sea level.

Whale Watching Cruises
Drive Time: Varies, depending on where you’re departing from (Dana Point, for example, is about 60 miles from DTLA)
Why We Love It: Living on a coast is good for more than just perennial beach days. Our ocean is teeming with life waiting to be discovered—and taking the kids out for a few hours on the waves means they might get that amazing thrill of spotting migrating whales—plus the resident sea lions, seals, and dolphins that make SoCal waters their year-round home.
When to go: Grey whale season runs from Dec. through Apr.; Blue whale season runs May through Nov.
There are several whale-watching outfits leaving out of LA-area harbors, including larger tour operators like Harbor Breeze Cruises and LA Waterfront, which offer two-story boats for $45 a person (if you book online you’ll save some money!). Or, if you want a more intimate experience, companies such as Captain Dave’s and Newport Coastal Adventures out of Dana Point and Newport Beach offer private trips if you’re willing to pay for the privacy; these tours range from about $71 per person for a Zodiac (up to 20 passengers) to $398 for a private charter (up to 6 people).

Travel
While Los Angeles offers a plethora of attractions—including beaches, museums, parks, and gardens—we could all do with a relaxing getaway from the big city now and then. Fortunately, the City of Angels is close to some of the coolest destinations in the Golden State, perfect for anyone who likes to get out and explore. If you want a full-day vacation, take a look at the best day trips from Los Angeles perfect for an out-of-this-world getaway.
Distance: 30 minutes by car
First up on our list of cool day trips from Los Angeles by car is the cozy getaway that is Santa Monica. Just a half-hour drive brings you to an iconic coastline is one of the closest Los Angeles getaways. You’re guaranteed to have fun on the roller coasters and bumper cars at Pacific Park on the Santa Monica Pier. Hit the arcade, win a prize, and enjoy panoramic views of the coast on the Pacific Ferris wheel.
When it’s time for a snack, treat yourself to the burger and pizza bars along the pier and finish off your meal with a creamy dessert at one of Santa Monica’s wonderful ice cream parlors. Then, head on down to the Santa Monica Pier Aquarium to catch a cool glimpse of life underwater. Wrap up your Santa Monica getaway with some luxury shopping at the Third Street Promenade.
Distance: 1 hour by car
A visit to Point Dume in Malibu is an easy affordable romantic getaway. Just one quick road trip from Los Angeles away, Malibu offers amazing beaches, high-class dining, and the luxuriant SoCal beach lifestyle. Have a delightful swim in the emerald blue waters of the Pacific and marvel at the beauty of Malidu’s sandy cliffside beaches. When dinner time rolls around, Malibu Farm Restaurant awaits you with its healthy eco-conscious menu and spectacular views from the pier.
Once you’ve had a chance to recharge at Malibu’s award-winning hotels, bask in the glory of the great outdoors while hiking to Escondido Falls. If you have some time to spare, pay a visit to Malibu Creek State Park—the best nature lovers’ destination for a fun day trip from Los Angeles.

Explore Huntington Central Park’s urban forest on horseback for a unique experience that transports you back in time. Enjoy great fishing with Wagner Charters, which also offers day trips to Catalina Island, another great destination for a last-minute trip from Los Angeles. For your last day at Huntington Beach, grab a juicy Billionaire burger made with Wagyu beef at Simmzy’s chich gastropub featuring unbeatable pier views.
